# Edit pace

**How often does something on screen change?** · [all approaches](index.md)


## Hyper: shots under 2 s
<a id="hyper"></a>

Shots of 0.8–1.8 s, push-ins, flashes and speed ramps on percussive hits.

**Looks like:** Trailer energy: every hit of the beat brings a new shot or push, with text slamming in. Done in 30–45 s.

**Good at:** thumb stop; teasers; energy

**Weak at:** exhausting over long runtimes; little room for teaching

**Best for:** formats reel30, yt-short · niches gym, gaming, all · goals reach · effort high

**How:** Cut to beat markers in CapCut; speed ramps on hits.

**Backed by:** [Sell a long video with a hyper-edited teaser](../topics/editing.md#edit-teaser-hyper-edited), [Speed ramps: dead time, beats, top rep](../topics/editing.md#edit-speed-ramps), [Kinetic type: float-ins, glow, pop-ins](../topics/effects.md#fx-kinetic-words), [Long-form talking pace 2.5–4.5 s](../topics/editing.md#edit-long-form-talking-pace), [Cut on the beat or on motion](../topics/editing.md#edit-cut-on-beat-motion) · sources L08

## Fast: a change every 1.2–2.5 s
<a id="fast"></a>

A cut, label, card or layout swap every 1.2–2.5 s, with no dead air.

**Looks like:** Breaths are cut and every couple of seconds a label pops, the layout flips or a card slides in. Talking, but never still.

**Good at:** retention; short-form teaching; proven in Rahul's sample

**Weak at:** more edit time; can feel frantic

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches all · goals retention · effort medium

**How:** Silence removal, then add a visual event every ~2 s on the timeline.

**Backed by:** [Something new on screen every 1.2–2.5 s](../topics/editing.md#edit-change-every-1-5-2-5s), [Cut every breath and pause](../topics/editing.md#edit-cut-breaths-no-dead-air), [Voice cadence as pattern interrupt](../topics/sound.md#sound-voice-cadence-interrupt), [Tool card lands on the word](../topics/text.md#l10-card-on-the-word), [Make motion visible with a dotted trail](../topics/effects.md#fx-trail-visual-proof) · sources L01, L02, R1

## Overlay-driven, slow camera
<a id="overlay-driven"></a>

Camera shots last ~10 s; overlays change about every 2 s.

**Looks like:** The same desk framing holds while cards, prompts and freezes come and go every couple of seconds. Calm but busy.

**Good at:** fast feel without jump cuts; polished tutorials; proof lands on the word

**Weak at:** graphic-heavy; needs a good static frame

**Best for:** formats reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches tech · goals retention, saves · effort high

**How:** Lock the camera; build the overlays in HyperFrames on word timings.

**Backed by:** [Tool card lands on the word](../topics/text.md#l10-card-on-the-word), [Pause-and-play breakdown of a reel](../topics/ideas.md#l10-pause-and-play-breakdown), [Graphic yap: one overlay every ~2 s](../topics/editing.md#edit-graphic-yap-overlay-2s), [Travel shots: silhouettes, backs, slow-mo](../topics/filming.md#film-travel-shots), [Live-build parts card with budget bar](../topics/effects.md#fx-live-build-parts-card) · sources L10

## Measured: 2.5–4.5 s shots
<a id="measured"></a>

Talking shots of 2.5–4.5 s, with axial jump cuts on emphasis words and longer holds for demos.

**Looks like:** A conversational rhythm; a punch-in on every few emphasis words and 8–15 s holds while something is demonstrated.

**Good at:** long-form watch time; comprehension; less fatigue

**Weak at:** can feel slow in short form; needs strong talking

**Best for:** formats reel90, yt-long · niches all · goals retention, trust · effort medium

**How:** Jump cuts every 3–6 words with digital punch-ins in CapCut/VN.

**Backed by:** [Long-form talking pace 2.5–4.5 s](../topics/editing.md#edit-long-form-talking-pace), [Axial jump cuts every 3–6 words](../topics/editing.md#edit-axial-jump-cuts), [Subtle 105–110% punch-in on key phrases](../topics/effects.md#fx-subtle-punch-in), [Hook window: 2–3 s short, 15–20 s long](../topics/hooks.md#hook-window-short-vs-long) · sources L06, L07

## Long takes
<a id="long-takes"></a>

Wide multi-cam with long uncut conversation; demos are the pattern interrupts.

**Looks like:** Two people talking in a wide shot for a minute at a time; occasionally a screen demo cuts in.

**Good at:** podcast feel; trust; minimal editing

**Weak at:** not for short-form feeds; needs good conversation

**Best for:** formats podcast, yt-long · niches all · goals trust, speed · effort low

**How:** Switch angles only on speaker changes.

**Backed by:** [Podcast body: long takes, demos as interrupts](../topics/editing.md#edit-podcast-long-takes), [Long-form talking pace 2.5–4.5 s](../topics/editing.md#edit-long-form-talking-pace), [Context in the first words, three channels](../topics/hooks.md#hook-context-first-words), [Cold open with later highlights](../topics/hooks.md#hook-cold-open-montage) · sources L08

## Mixing
Train a regular rhythm, then break it for the big moment. Long pieces can open hyper (the teaser) and settle into measured.

## Rule of thumb
Teasers: hyper. Short teaching: fast or overlay-driven. Long form: measured. Podcasts: long takes.
